purpose: Web UI for visualizing and querying data stored in Elasticsearch.
description: Kibana is a full read/query interface into whatever Elasticsearch cluster it's connected to. Left exposed without authentication (its default configuration has none — auth is only enforced when X-Pack/Elastic security features are explicitly enabled), it gives anyone who can reach it the ability to browse, query, and often export every index the cluster holds.
common_risks: no authentication on the Kibana UI or its underlying Elasticsearch cluster
full data exposure via Dev Tools / Discover
outdated Kibana versions with known RCE issues
misconfigurations: xpack.security.enabled left false (or the free security features never turned on)
Kibana exposed directly to the internet instead of behind a VPN/auth proxy
attack_patterns: Browse indices directly through Discover or Dev Tools with no login required
Use Dev Tools to run arbitrary Elasticsearch queries against every index the cluster holds
Exploit known Kibana RCE vulnerabilities on outdated, internet-facing instances
real_world_incidents: Unauthenticated Kibana/Elasticsearch pairs are a recurring source of large-scale data exposure incidents in cloud misconfiguration research, frequently surfacing logs, PII, or application data indexed for analytics.
recommended_actions: Enable Elastic's security features (authentication) on both Elasticsearch and Kibana — this has been free since the 7.1 default distribution.
Never expose Kibana directly to the internet; put it behind a VPN, SSO proxy, or at minimum an authenticating reverse proxy.
Keep Kibana patched — several versions have had disclosed RCE vulnerabilities reachable pre-authentication.
Restrict which indices each authenticated role can query, rather than granting blanket access.

audience_guidance.student: Kibana is a dashboard for exploring data stored in Elasticsearch — think of it as a window into a big searchable database. If that window has no lock on it, anyone who finds the URL can browse everything behind it.
audience_guidance.developer: Turn on Elastic's built-in security features (they're free) so Kibana and Elasticsearch both require authentication, and never expose Kibana directly to the public internet.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: An unauthenticated Kibana is almost always a serious finding — confirm access via Discover or Dev Tools and note the scope of indices visible.
audience_guidance.pentester: Use Dev Tools to enumerate indices and extract representative sensitive data as impact evidence; check the Kibana version against known pre-auth RCE advisories.
audience_guidance.security_team: Treat any internet-facing Kibana without authentication as a critical incident — audit your Elastic Stack deployments for security-feature status and network exposure.
